children: Hirata will initially bring its standard semiconductor automation portfolio to India, targeting OSAT, advanced packaging and wafer and panel handling

Japanese automation and semiconductor equipment manufacturer Hirata Corporation has entered the Indian market through a strategic partnership with ATS India, which will serve as its exclusive distribution partner for semiconductor equipment and technology in the country.

The partnership comes as India works to expand its domestic semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging capabilities ahead of hosting Semicon India 2026. Hirata will initially focus on bringing its standard product portfolio to Indian manufacturers, with customised and application-specific solutions expected to follow as the market develops.

The partnership builds on an existing relationship between Hirata and ATS spanning more than a decade across sectors including automotive. The companies will now extend that relationship to semiconductor manufacturing, with a focus on backend and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) operations, advanced packaging, and wafer and panel handling.

Hirata's portfolio to be distributed in India includes Equipment Front End Modules (EFEM), FOPLP Load Ports, PLP Panel Handling Robots, and high-performance wafer handling robots. The equipment is designed for wafer and panel handling across semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging processes.

Kishen Kavikondala, CEO, ATS India, said the initial focus would be on establishing the commercial, technical and service infrastructure required as India's semiconductor manufacturing capacity expands.

“The focus of this partnership is on building the local commercial, technical and service ecosystem that Indian semiconductor manufacturers will need as their capacity grows over the next decade,” Kavikondala said.

He added that the companies would focus initially on precision manufacturing solutions before moving towards more customised offerings as the market matures. “By making Hirata's advanced equipment locally available, semiconductor and electronics manufacturers in India will no longer need to depend on cross-border logistics or delayed technical support that have historically slowed adoption,” he said.

John Derzy, Vice President, Hirata Corporation of America, said India is an important growth market as semiconductor and electronics manufacturing diversifies globally. “India represents one of the most important growth markets for Hirata as global semiconductor and electronics manufacturing continues to diversify,” Derzy said.

“A larger goal underpinning this partnership is bringing greater automation to semiconductor manufacturing processes in India, particularly across OSAT operations, which remain largely manual or semi-automated in the Indian context today,” Derzy said.

Derzy added automation would be a key differentiator for Hirata in the Indian market. “Over the next two to three years, we expect this collaboration to fundamentally change how Indian manufacturers access and adopt advanced semiconductor equipment technology,” he said.

The partnership comes as India's electronic manufacturing services (EMS) industry expands beyond assembly-led manufacturing towards components, engineering and higher-complexity production. The Indian EMS market is expected to exceed USD 150 billion by FY30, compared with an estimated USD 40-45 billion in 2025, according to the companies.

For ATS India and Hirata, the focus will be on the semiconductor segment of this broader manufacturing expansion, particularly equipment and automation for backend manufacturing and advanced packaging. The companies said the partnership would also support local skill development and the wider precision-manufacturing supply chain.

ATS India said Hirata's standard products would be introduced first, with the companies planning to expand into application-specific and customised solutions as India's semiconductor ecosystem matures.
